findings.claim: An overlay sidebar opened in focus mode stays open after leaving (by T or the tree button) whenever the sidebar is in overlay form for another reason (viewport below 1200px, or the tree beside/yielded), because SidebarProvider only closes it when isOverlay flips and focusLent does not flip isOverlay there.
findings.impact: At 1024px (or at 1440 with the tree shown) a viewer who opens the menu in the revealed header and then presses T, or presses the tree button (z-50, above the z-30 backdrop), leaves focus mode with the overlay sidebar still open over the ordinary page. The same gap means an overlay sidebar that is open when T enters focus mode at <1200px is not closed on entering (spec §1.3).
findings.evidence: SidebarProvider.tsx:60 isOverlay = routeOverlay || focusLent || narrow; SidebarProvider.tsx:76-83 setIsOpen(false) runs only in a layout effect keyed on isOverlay; useFocusSidebarWhen (SidebarProvider.tsx:190-195) only toggles focusLent. With narrow=true (NARROW_QUERY max-width 1199px) or routeOverlay=true (TwoPaneLayout.tsx:135 useOverlaySidebarWhen(treeBeside || yielded)) isOverlay stays true across entering/leaving, so isOpen is never reset. The overlay sidebar's shortcut context (Sidebar.tsx:290-295) has no blocksLower, and canTakeFocusModeShortcut excludes data-app-sidebar, so T fires with it open. The only test (focus-mode-desktop.spec.ts 'T with the overlay sidebar open leaves focus mode') runs at 1280 with the tree hidden, where isOverlay does flip.
findings.repro: Traced statically, not run: open focus-drive at 1024×900, file=video; press the Focus mode button; reveal with the pointer at the top; click Menu (overlay opens, aria-pressed=true); press T. Expected per I4: overlay closed. Traced: focusLent false, narrow still true, isOverlay unchanged, layout effect does not run, isOpen remains true, so the menu button stays aria-pressed=true and the overlay stays drawn.

bucket_proposal.reason: I4: 'an overlay sidebar opened in focus mode is closed on leaving by either path'.

findings.proposed_fix: In the focus-layout transition (useFocusSidebarWhen or SidebarProvider), call setIsOpen(false) when focusLent changes in either direction while isOverlay stays true. Then add the 1024px and tree-shown rows to the overlay-close test.

findings.claim: On a /drive/{drive}?file=… URL whose drive layout draws DriveUnavailable, T still toggles focus mode on, because FocusModeShortcuts is active on isFilePageUrl (pure URL test) and DriveUnavailable only clears the store once on mount.
findings.impact: On the 'Can't open the drive' screen, T hides the header and sidebar, and the screen has no Focus mode button. The cheat sheet also lists T there. The viewer has to press T again or reveal the header to recover.
findings.evidence: AppShell.tsx:334 <FocusModeShortcuts active={filePageUrl} />; useFocusMode.ts:15-22 isFilePageUrl is true for any /drive/… with a file param; DriveUnavailable.tsx:29-31 useLayoutEffect(() => focusModeStore.set(false), []) runs only on mount; AppShell.tsx:288-290 resets the store only when filePageUrl changes. The spec's Terms say such a URL is not a file page URL. No test covers DriveUnavailable at all, so deleting DriveUnavailable.tsx:29-31 survives every spec in the diff.
findings.repro: Traced statically, not run: open /drive/x?file=y where drive x is unavailable; press T with nothing focused. Traced: toggleFocusMode → store true → useFocusLayout true (file page URL and wide) → the header becomes data-focus-header=hidden and html gets data-focus-layout over DriveUnavailable.

bucket_proposal.reason: I4 requires the focus state to be off whenever the URL is not a file page URL. The spec defines a DriveUnavailable URL as not a file page URL, so I6's T toggle must not apply there.

findings.proposed_fix: Make the 'not a file page' fact available to useIsFilePageUrl and FocusModeShortcuts, for example through a flag that DriveUnavailable sets while mounted, instead of a one-shot store reset. Add a test that presses T on DriveUnavailable.

findings.claim: toggleFocusMode always captures a reading anchor, but restoreReadingAnchor runs only when focusLayout changes, so an anchor captured by T below 768px stays pending and is applied later when the viewport widens.
findings.impact: On a phone-width window or an iPad in portrait: the viewer presses T, scrolls elsewhere, then widens or rotates to landscape. The content jumps back to where it was when T was pressed.
findings.evidence: useFocusMode.ts:92-95 rememberReadingAnchor() on every toggle; readingAnchor.ts:120-123 sets module-level pending; AppShell.tsx:311-313 restoreReadingAnchor only in an effect keyed on focusLayout, which does not change when T is pressed below 768px (useFocusLayout requires wide); readingAnchor.ts:131-180 then scrolls the remembered element back over up to 20 frames.
findings.repro: Traced statically, not run: at 700px on a scrolled PDF file page, press T (state on, layout unchanged, pending captured). Scroll the pane by several pages, then widen to 1280. focusLayout becomes true and restoreReadingAnchor scrolls back to the T-time element.

bucket_proposal.reason: I2 and I5 do not cover reading position across a resize. The behaviour is wrong but breaks no declared invariant.

findings.proposed_fix: Capture the anchor only when the toggle will change focusLayout, or drop a pending anchor on the next user scroll.

findings.claim: Unplanned place: frontend/src/lib/readingAnchor.ts is a new module that is not in the touch-point list. It writes scrollTop on any detected scroller, or calls window.scrollBy, for up to 20 frames after every focus-layout change.
findings.impact: Every focus-layout change, including resizes across 768px and leaving by navigation, now scrolls the page programmatically. No invariant covers its side effects beyond I2's reading-position clause; F3 is one consequence.
findings.evidence: readingAnchor.ts:131-180; called from useFocusMode.ts:93 and AppShell.tsx:311-313. The touch points list neither file nor a scroll-restoring mechanism.

bucket_proposal.reason: A reach outside the touch-point list, and a candidate for a missing invariant: the restore must not move the scroll except across a press that changes the layout.

findings.claim: Unplanned place: frontend/src/lib/safeArea.ts is a new module that is not in the touch-point list. Header calls it on every ResizeObserver callback in the focus layout, and it appends and removes a probe div on document.body each time.
findings.impact: Each call is a body childList mutation, which AppShell's document-wide MutationObserver (AppShell.tsx:180-186) re-evaluates as a possible cover. It is harmless today but couples the two.

bucket_proposal.reason: A reach outside the touch-point list; no invariant broken.

findings.claim: Unplanned places: frontend/src/components/FocusModeShortcuts.tsx and frontend/src/components/FileDetail/FocusModeButton.tsx are new files that are not in the touch-point list. The plan put the focus-mode shortcut context in useFocusMode.ts and the button in FileDetailChrome.tsx.
findings.impact: None for a user. The behaviour lives where the plan did not say.
findings.evidence: FocusModeShortcuts.tsx:15-32 (mounted at AppShell.tsx:334); FocusModeButton.tsx:9-29 (used at FileDetailChrome.tsx:146).

bucket_proposal.reason: A file-level reach outside the list. The behaviour matches the planned touch points.

findings.claim: Unplanned behaviour at a listed place: DriveUnavailable.tsx is listed only as a user of h-below-header that keeps its height, but the diff makes it write the focus store.
findings.impact: It becomes part of focus mode's lifetime rule, and an incomplete one (see F2).

bucket_proposal.reason: Reach beyond the planned role of a listed file.

findings.claim: Unplanned places: shared component-test infrastructure that every fixture uses is changed, and none of it is in the touch-point list or §7: e2e-components/stubs/next-navigation.ts, fixtures/app.tsx, fixtures/inspectorResponsive.tsx (exports), projects.ts and spec-viewport.spec.ts.
findings.impact: The router stub now subscribes every usePathname/useSearchParams reader to a store. It also returns one shared EMPTY_QUERY instance instead of a fresh URLSearchParams per call, so effects keyed on searchParams in other fixtures now run less often. That can change what unrelated existing component specs observe.
findings.evidence: stubs/next-navigation.ts:22-56; inspectorResponsive.tsx installFetch/installMedia/VIDEO_ID/PDF_ID now exported; projects.ts and spec-viewport.spec.ts list the two new specs.

findings.claim: Unplanned places: existing tests that §7 does not list are modified: e2e-components/file-header-row.spec.ts, src/components/__tests__/AppShell.quickNote.test.tsx and src/components/__tests__/MenuButton.test.tsx.
findings.impact: None found. The changes add one assertion (narrow: no Focus mode button) and mocks (useSearchParams, useFocusSidebarWhen, setFocusLent, useShortcutsContext). No assertion is weakened.
findings.evidence: Diff hunks of the three files; MenuButton.test.tsx:8-39.

findings.claim: Reach beyond the planned scope of globals.css: html[data-focus-settling] * { transition: none !important } cancels every transition in the document for one frame. AppShell sets it on mount (every app load) and on every focus-layout change, not only for the sidebar, tree and header named in the plan.
findings.impact: Any unrelated transition in flight at that frame (inspector, toasts, sheets) snaps. Low visible effect.
findings.evidence: globals.css:717-720; AppShell.tsx:292-307 (the effect also runs on mount with focusLayout=false).

specification_compliance: Places reached outside the touch-point list: lib/readingAnchor.ts, lib/safeArea.ts, components/FocusModeShortcuts.tsx, components/FileDetail/FocusModeButton.tsx, DriveUnavailable's write to the focus store, the shared e2e-components infrastructure (stubs/next-navigation.ts, fixtures/app.tsx, fixtures/inspectorResponsive.tsx, projects.ts, spec-viewport.spec.ts), and the existing tests file-header-row.spec.ts, AppShell.quickNote.test.tsx and MenuButton.test.tsx.

TwoPaneLayout covers CollectionDetail's left pane. HighlightControls has no popover trigger, so it needs no aria-expanded. useInspectorFit sees offsetWidth 0 for the w-0 pane, so no yield is recorded.
I4 is broken below 1200px or with the tree beside or yielded: the overlay sidebar is not closed on leaving (F1).
I4/I6: T re-enters focus mode on a DriveUnavailable screen at a ?file= URL (F2).

I9: the button is drawn on all three hosts' loaded and failed paths (RightPaneFile.tsx:101-113, FileDetailFullScreen.tsx:326-336). The header-row-missing fixture, which renders FileDetailContent with no host, is not a production path.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The reading-anchor restore scrolls after any focus-layout change, including resizes across 768px, with an anchor captured possibly long before (F3).
isHeaderMenuOpen matches any header element in the document. A PageHeader <header> with an expanded control would also suppress T and hold the reveal.
The mutation observer over the whole documentElement re-checks the cover on every subtree childList change while in the focus layout.
regression_risks: SidebarProvider's overlay effect moved from useEffect to useLayoutEffect, so the timing of every overlay flip changes, including the narrow media query, the tree borrow and FileDetailFullScreen's borrow, not only focus mode.
After this change canTakeFindShortcut yields under ConfirmDialog, RenameDialog and the desktop GlobalSearch window, which affects find and FileDetailShell's canTakeFind.

The transition kill-switch on AppShell mount affects the first frame of every load.

No test covers DriveUnavailable with focus mode; deleting DriveUnavailable.tsx:29-31 would survive (F2).
No test covers T below 768px followed by a scroll and then widening (F3).
